reviews.boundary_analysis: Approved-workflow exception, lockfile-commit instruction and protected-branch nonrewrite treatment differ from canonical explicit-request-only rule. All are already registered, including uncertainty; no new claim.

Single-branch normal-worktree restriction and branch naming/granularity details extend canonical isolation, but already captured. No unconditional separate-worktree requirement is inferred from branches-or-worktrees.

Canonical three-way decision approval does not entail fixed slots, exhaustive contract replacement, exact facet paths, options/report fields, valid dated lexical approval tokens or reopening all register decisions. Each extension is already explicit in the union. Executable constraints inspected separately from prose: preflight blocks undiscovered/no-edge cases, post-tool findings depend on attributable baseline/HEAD differences, token recognition ignores approval negation. Already BF0192/BF0143/BF0124. No new interpretation promoted.

Never silently rewrite/ignore user requirement is additional to canonical challenge-and-alternative, but both explicit records include it. Workflow referral does not make every routine change a Decision Request.
No automatic stashing and no removal of worktree with uncommitted user work narrow convenience operations beyond data destruction; explicit coverage already exists, including preservation precheck.
High-risk lost/rewritten-content inspection, push verification/scope and intended-combined conflict behavior extend minimum-operation state inspection; all registered with correct lifecycle.

Propagation avoids unrelated numeric matches, keeps backend validation authoritative, rechecks spec and reports every updated surface. These subclauses and hook reminder/filtering behavior are already registered; no new clause.
